children: Each of Canada's big bank's beat consensus expectations for fiscal 3Q, yet most stocks traded lower. TD Cowen suggests valuation played a role, as did poor earnings quality and a growing awareness that topline growth could slow materially as trading conditions normalize. TD says it doesn't support the narrative that credit was an issue for the banks, since impaired provisions for credit losses fell and consumer delinquencies improved in the important unsecured category. That said, TD reckons Bank of Nova Scotia appears to be on the mend, with the resumption of balance sheet growth the key indicator it needed to see to support moving to a buy call from hold with a target of C$141 from C$124 previously. (robb.stewart@wsj.com)
